featured_reviews.review_text: Spenta is a 'must go to travel partner' for holidays around the world.  Our Bhutan trip was a well planned group tour, with all comforts on offer; great food, good hotels and their excellent team to guide us through our holiday.

featured_reviews.name: Anahita Bamboat
featured_reviews.review_text:
I will start off this review with a heartfelt thanks to our ever smiling and hospitable Hoshang & Tanaz for a wonderful holiday in Georgia!! :) This was our first time travelling with Spenta and my husband and I absolutely loved it! We felt so welcome and everyone was like a family having fun, taking care of each other. At first I was a bit apprehensive as most of the times we have travelled alone and never really done group tours, that too with most of the members being senior citizens; but we were in for a pleasant surprise. The tour was well organised and paced. We never had to worry about the rooms or the luggage, transport etc. Everything  was looked after and we had to just follow the lead. We felt the warmth in the small thoughtful gestures like arranging for snacks for our flights, bus trips, the introductory call with all group members explaining all the details, what to expect, what to carry, the expected weather etc. Special mention to the lavish, king size wonderful tables set up for us for each and every meal! I personally thoroughly enjoyed the variety of local cuisine and always look forward to them ( I can make do without even the 2 Indian meals we had!). Will always remember the various Khachapuris and the juicy, moist Khinkalis and all our jokes over the khachapuris! Fresh produce, fresh salads and fruits...a lovely treat to the tastebuds and accumulation of some more fat! Another special shout out to our friendly, patient and smiling local tour guide Luca who always had a helping hand & had a bunch of historical stories & jokes ready for us!
Coming to Georgia....She is old, refined and beautiful! She has the most varied topography from lovely rolling hills, the Caucasus range of mountains, to the flat lands and the beaches! Her churches are simple and a stark contrast from the ornate, elaborate and colourful ones I have seen across Prague and various cities of Austria. There is a lot to see from the Statue of Ali & Nino, to Martvili and Prometheus Caves (quite a marvel), Giuaani winery, Chronicles of Georgia to the various churches/monasteries. I specially enjoyed the early morning Tbilisi walking tour where i saw another artistic side of the city with art in all the smallest nooks & corners!
To sum up....I didn't expect much out of this tour, but we both went back with happy and fun memories of a wonderful, much needed break! Look forward to more holidays with Spenta! Mahdlohba! [I hope I got it right]

featured_reviews.review_text:
A Life-Changing Experience with Gufram — The Heart of Mumbai

If you visit Mumbai, please, do yourself a favor and meet Gufram. I have traveled a lot, but I have never met a guide like him — kind, humble, unbelievably knowledgeable, and so deeply connected to the real life of this city.

From the moment you meet him, you feel safe, welcomed, and understood. He knows everything: history, culture, hidden corners, local habits — and he gives you advice with so much patience and honesty. He is funny, full of stories, speaks many languages, and is even learning Polish!

But the experience that touched me the most was the real slum tour — something I will remember for the rest of my life.
This is not a tourist show. This is real Mumbai. Real people. Real stories.

Gufram is the founder of the SlumCare Foundation, and every tour supports his community. He shares his own journey too — arriving in Mumbai at 15 with nothing but dreams to support his family, and working hard ever since. Listening to him while walking through the narrow lanes… it is impossible not to feel it deeply.

He also took me to the incredible outdoor laundry where most of Mumbai’s hotels wash their linens — an entire world of hard work and resilience. Seeing all of this with Gufram’s explanations made everything so raw, so human, so emotional.

This tour left me speechless. Truly. It changed the way I see Mumbai, India, and even my own life.
It made me grateful, humble, and open in a new way.

If you come to Mumbai, do not leave without doing this tour.
Be open, be brave, and let Gufram show you the Mumbai that travelers rarely see.

It is not just a tour.
It is an experience that stays in your heart forever.

If you have the opportunity, take the "slum" tour.  Goofy lives in one of the slums with his family and runs a charitable classroom to support the education of the children who live there. featured_reviews.name: שגיא פרידמן
featured_reviews.review_text:
We landed in Mumbai wanting the most authentic tour possible—not just touristy spots, but a peek into the city's cultural richness, local food, and impoverished neighborhoods where life pulses with passion despite harsh poverty. We chose Gufi (Guran), who came highly recommended. Lucky for us!
Gufi picked us up in his "Slum-borghini" (wait till you see it). From the start, we knew this was different. He shared his deep connection with Israelis and genuinely looked forward to meeting us—not just for work, but for a heart-to-heart connection. We met a charismatic storyteller with fascinating knowledge and tremendous motivation to tailor the tour perfectly.
The most meaningful place was Gufi's neighborhood in the slums—Dhobi Ghat, an authentic hand laundry. Everyone knows and appreciates Gufi. The contrast captivated us: a difficult place where you feel the lack, yet filled with joy, warmth, and community. It put things in perspective—what are we complaining about, and how privileged we are?
Poverty alongside bustling life, welcoming people smiling, proud to shake our hands. Single-room apartments, vendors in narrow alleys, colorful shops, children running after us wanting only our attention.
But Gufi isn't just a tour guide—he's an educational leader in his neighborhood (where hundreds of thousands live in an impossibly small area). A changemaker bringing inspiration.
With extremely limited resources, he established an educational center teaching children English for social mobility. He created a soccer team to incentivize attendance. From the tour fee (modest for what you receive!), Gufi allocates 40% to the center. What a moving person!
Gufi sleeps with his family on two mattresses but doesn't complain. With a sparkle in his eyes, he captivates us with graciousness and humility. He's grateful, showing how true richness comes from within. Non-judgmental, he fulfilled all our wishes and took us to the most authentic, delicious places.
The tour includes about 10 destinations, but it's flexible based on your desires and energy. We felt no time pressure, giving us full value.
One unforgettable moment—after 7 hours, we stopped at Victoria Railway Station for vada pav and samosas. Gufi treated us generously. When I suggested saving leftovers for his children, he smiled and pointed to a small homeless girl (about 4), her mother sleeping on the sidewalk. He said: Go, give her the food. It's good karma.
I'll never forget her big eyes looking into mine, understanding, her smile and "Namaste," and the approving nods from everyone around. Even writing this moves me. Gufi isn't just a tour guide... The Talmud says whoever saves one life saves an entire world—Gufi has tremendous merit for countless souls he's saved and will save. He came to see others with compassion, not to escape his hardship but to change it.
We were fortunate to see Mumbai through his good eyes. Highly recommend him! Already waiting for next time!
